title: Book Two · Chapter 9: The Same Blue Cover
story:
The second box has more books.

Jun opens it on Tuesday. He takes out a red book, then two blue ones.

Ronan puts the blue books together. Their covers look almost the same.

“Two copies,” he says.

Mei turns one over.

“No. This one is about a river.”

“So is that one.”

“Look inside.”

One book has a boat on the first page. The other begins with a small house beside the water.

Ronan reads the titles again. The last words are different.

He puts a little space between the books.

“I thought we could put one away.”

“Both can stay,” Mei says. “I want to read about the house.”

Leo is looking for the train book. He finds it on the right side of the shelf.

“Can I borrow it now?”

Miss Wu checks her little list. “Not yet. We are still checking the pages.”

Leo opens the book to the middle. A page is loose. He holds it very carefully.

“This one needs help.”

Miss Wu takes it to her desk. The loose page has a picture of a station.

“My dad works near one of those,” Leo says.

Ronan comes over to look. In the picture, a woman holds a case. A boy stands beside a window.

“Is he going away?” Ronan asks.

“The story will tell us,” Miss Wu says. “Let us finish the page first.”

She shows them a thin strip of paper for the broken edge. Leo holds the page still. Ronan brings a clean cloth for the table. Miss Wu does the repair herself.

The book stays open to dry.

At the shelf, Jun puts one book in the wrong pile. Ronan starts to correct him, then looks more closely.

The front has a tree. But the story is about a family, not a garden.

They take it to Mei. She opens the first page.

“Put it here for now. We can change the groups later.”

They do not need a new label for every book today.

At lunch, Ronan looks at the two blue covers again. He reads both titles aloud. This time he reaches the last word on each one.

Mei picks up the river-house book. She finds a picture of a kitchen with a round window.

“I like that window.”

“For your room?”

“For a drawing.”

She takes a scrap of paper from her own bag. Ronan does not ask her to draw the whole house for him. He gets the other blue book and sits nearby.

There is a little boat under a bridge. He can read the line below it. He turns the page and finds the boat again, now beside the bank.

Leo finishes lunch. Then he comes over. He looks at both books, then at Mei's paper.

“Is there a train in either one?”

“No,” Ronan says.

Leo sits down anyway. He reads the first part of the boat story with him. When the bell rings, they leave their paper markers in two different places.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

copy＝同一本的另一本；title＝书名；loose＝松开的；case＝箱子。

## 理解问题

1. 两个蓝封面的书为什么都要留下？
2. 火车书为什么暂时不能借走？

## 读句子

The last words / are different.＝最后的词／不一样。
